title: The comparison harness of the team arms: rules, helper and agent brains on the same written cases, scored by code from the records
request: Package B4 of the team workspace plan (Part B, step 8): build dclab_rnd/agent_eval/team_arms/ in the shape of planning_gate_v3 (pinned terms, a sealed run-once marker, no Claude model anywhere, caps, the plan printed before spending). A case format (pydantic with a JSON Schema) and a guide (CASES.md) so an independent author writes the dev and sealed sets; a runner that plays one case under one arm on a fresh workspace through the real team runtime with scripted people, every model call through the gateway under agent_runs/live_tests/<run>/ with thinking kept whole; a scorer that is code only from the records (main score, seven hard zeros, counts); an optional free non-Claude judge; a comparison report with bootstrap intervals into evidence/campaigns/team_arms_v1/; the winner rule pinned by hash (team_arms_gate_v1); a CLI plan|run|report. The builder writes only a 3-case smoke file; no live model is called (the owner runs the live comparisons).
spec: New package dclab_rnd/agent_eval/team_arms/: cases.py (Case, CaseSet, Reply with triggers question/team_question/report, Expected with end answer/blocker/question/refused, facts, answer_holds_any/answer_lacks_any, traps; MANIFEST pins dev and sealed by sha256), play.py (Player: lead.ask or agents.from_thread, delivery.run until settled, scripted replies through lead.answer, from_thread, confirm_outcome, correct; ArmGateway giving only the team purposes the run's model, capped by RunBudget, refusing Claude models and endpoints; DCLAB_TEAM_BRAIN for the roles under test; a unique workspace folder per play), text.py (the scorer's own pinned copy of the number, sentence and claim rules), score.py (Records; hard zeros invented_number, unrecorded_claim, unauthorised_read, agent_approved, customer_contacted, holdout_twice, answer_not_given; main score; counts), gate.py (terms, fingerprint over the rule, limits and the deciding code, pin, arm_summary, winner, bootstrap), report.py, judge.py (the harness ablation's judge prompt reused, blind), __init__.py (CLI, run_cases with resume, thinking_check, sealed marker), CASES.md, cases/quick_example.json (smoke, never scored), cases/case_set.schema.json, gate_v1.sha256; evidence/campaigns/team_arms_v1/manifest.json; tests/test_team_arms.py.
plan: read the plan's B4 row, planning_gate_v3's code (never its held files), the harness ablation's gateway, cap, judge and capture helpers, the team runtime (lead, agents, delivery, commercial, seats, agent_arm, store) and the team tests' setup
prototype a rules journey through the Lead and dump every record the scorer could read (tasks, actions, reports, deliveries, threads, events)

write the case format, then the runner, then the scorer, and sweep nine rules journeys (renewal, cancellations, recent, no dates, dispatch with a kitchen correction, Marketing terms, Sales capacity 0, an approve/contact order, an outcome correction) for false hard zeros
write the gate, the report, the judge and the CLI; pin the gate

write tests/test_team_arms.py: format and schema, the three smoke cases under R, H and A with scripted models, every hard zero planted, the main score, the winner rule and ties, the pin, sealed run-once, Claude refused, the cap, thinking checked
run the tests on files and with run_parallel.py --pg; review with dclab-reviewer; fix every finding with a test; re-review
second review (FAIL, N1 to N8): fix each with a test, re-pin, re-run on files and PostgreSQL, re-review
third review (N1 to N8 confirmed; M1 to M4 new): fix each with a test, re-pin, re-run on files and PostgreSQL, re-review

decisions.decision: Plays run through the product's own entry points (lead.ask, agents.from_thread, lead.answer, commercial answers through from_thread, confirm_outcome, correct) and the outbox (delivery.run), never by calling the agents' functions directly
decisions.why: the comparison must measure what the product does; a harness-only path would hide guard, delivery and lease behaviour

decisions.decision: The rules arm gets no gateway; the model arms get a view that serves only team_helper and team_agent
decisions.why: same everything but the brain: the rules arm can ask no model, so no other purpose may get one on the model arms either (the review's F15)

decisions.decision: What the people said is read only from the script's own record (play.json), never from the workspace
decisions.why: a model can write a message that looks like a person's; the answer_not_given check must compare with what was really sent

decisions.decision: Model-written text is identified structurally: an agent-arm report carries code's exact AGENT_LINE in its limits, its findings precede code's last 'From the records' separator; helper notes and every clarification are checked too
decisions.why: the scorer cannot trust the model's words to say which words are the model's; a model limit that only starts like the line stays model text

decisions.decision: Known numbers come only from primary records: the people's words, action records, evidence, fixtures, revisions, and the code-written text of reports that join no other report
decisions.why: joining reports copy children's answers (the rules' join, the agent arm's lines from the records); taking them as records laundered a model's invented number (the review's F2)

decisions.decision: A handed-out task's question is checked for numbers no record nor its parent's question holds
decisions.why: rules code quotes a child task's question in its report (ML Engineering's prediction moment): an agent Lead's invented number would otherwise reach the person through a rules template

decisions.decision: Reuse the harness ablation's judge prompt (ablation_judge) and map understanding, planning and evidence_discipline to understanding, plan and report
decisions.why: no new prompt (no agent-eval rerun needed), and it is the rubric the Nemotron judge already used in the earlier exams; the judge stays advisory

decisions.decision: The winner rule requires the rules arm to have played the role to the end with no hard zero; an equal main score goes to the simpler arm; the paired bootstrap interval against the rules is reported as within_noise
decisions.why: the default stays rules until a comparison says otherwise; a model arm must beat the rules, not an empty column (the review's F5)

decisions.decision: A run may resume in new sittings, each capped at 0.5 euro; complete plays are kept, cut ones kept aside and replayed; the sealed run resumes only as the run its marker names and is reported only when finished
decisions.why: about 350 sealed plays cannot fit one 0.5 euro run; without a resume the marker would burn the sealed set (the review's F4)

decisions.decision: The cap holds by a margin of one request's upper bound and by noticing a refusal for the run's money
decisions.why: the gateway refuses a request whose upper bound passes what is left, so a run just under its cap would have turned every model arm into the rules while the plays counted as complete (the review's F3)

decisions.decision: The gate's hash covers the scorer, runner, case format, gate, CLI, report, judge, cited.py and team_brain.py, and the scorer keeps its own copy of the identifier rule
decisions.why: tuning an arm on the dev set must never silently change what the scorer reads (the review's F10)

decisions.decision: The scorer reads numbers, sentences and claimed actions with its own copy (team_arms/text.py), and the gate's hash covers that copy, never cited.py or team_brain.py
decisions.why: B5 edits team_brain.py: a hash over shared files would block every report and a sealed resume, and a shared rule tuned for the arms would silently change the scorer (the re-review's N1)

decisions.decision: A resumed run replays only plays cut by the cap (or never ended); a crash, a failed delivery or a score error is final; it runs only on the code and pinned cases its first sitting recorded
decisions.why: a replay of a failed play is a second try for the model arms, and a repeating crash would block the sealed result forever (N2)

decisions.decision: An expected value must be told to the person and be in a code-written record, matched whole
decisions.why: a value only in the tree's records is not an answer the person got; '12' must never match '1200' or an id (N3, N4)

decisions.decision: A run's code is one hash over the contents of the files the arms and the scorer run on (team runtime, harness, team prompts, team contracts, agent loop, gateway), the commit kept for information
decisions.why: a commit or a file becoming tracked changes nothing a play does, so it must never block a resume; a real content change must (the third review's M1)

change: New: dclab_rnd/agent_eval/team_arms/{__init__,__main__,cases,play,score,gate,report,judge}.py, CASES.md, gate_v1.sha256, cases/{quick_example.json, MANIFEST.json, case_set.schema.json}; evidence/campaigns/team_arms_v1/manifest.json; tests/test_team_arms.py. outcome: The harness exists and is pinned (team_arms_gate_v1). The first dev comparison has not run: the dev and sealed sets are for an independent author, and the live runs are the owner's.
lessons: A scorer that reads text must know who wrote each word; structure written by code is a safer marker than any phrase, and copies are never records
Every guard that ends a run (a cap, a marker) needs a way to finish the work it interrupts, or it destroys the measurement it protects
On PostgreSQL a folder's path names its workspace: a harness that reuses a path reuses the workspace
Sweep the rules arm for false hard zeros before trusting a hard-zero check
A gate must hash only code it owns: a pin over a shared library becomes a lock on everyone else's work
A content hash meant to say 'the same code' must hash only code: a machine writes more than a person does
risks: The judge's plan score favours arms that write a plan the person sees
Arms with background helper threads may go slightly over a cap between checks
bench.LAYER_OF needs team_arms_v1 before the first dev report can be written
